facts.statement: Sveltonectes is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs from the Early Cretaceous of western Russia.
facts.quote: Sveltonectes (meaning "agile swimmer" in Greek) is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaurs known from Ul'yanovsk region, western Russia.

facts.statement: The genus is known from holotype IRSNB R269, an almost complete skeleton with a partial skull preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: Sveltonectes is known from the holotype IRSNB R269, an almost complete three-dimensionally preserved skeleton including a partial skull.

facts.statement: Fossils date to the late Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 126 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in unnamed locality, in Ul'yanovsk, dating to the late Barremian stage of the early Cretaceous, about 126 million years ago.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Fischer, Masure, Arkhangelsky, and Godefroit in 2011, with Sveltonectes insolitus as the type species.
facts.quote: Sveltonectes was named by Valentin Fischer, Edwige Masure, Maxim S. Arkhangelsky, and Pascal Godefroit in 2011 and the type species is Sveltonectes insolitus.

facts.statement: The specific name means "unusual" and refers to the animal's numerous unusual features and tooth morphology.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from insolitus, Latin for "unusual", in reference to the numerous unusual features of this ichthyosaur, as well as its unusual tooth morphology.

facts.statement: It is unique among its relatives for having small, sharp teeth and a very primitive prootic bone.
facts.quote: Sveltonectes is unique in that it has small, sharp teeth and numerous other peculiar features such as a very primitive prootic.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Sveltonectes as most closely related to Aegirosaurus within the family Ophthalmosauridae.
facts.quote: Within the Ophthalmosauridae, Sveltonectes is most closely related to Aegirosaurus.

facts.statement: It is classified within the subfamily Platypterygiinae of the family Ophthalmosauridae.
The time range for the genus is estimated between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The generic name is derived from sveltos, Greek for "agile", and nektes, Greek for "swimmer", and refers to its small size, streamlined skull, and powerful girdle musculature.
